body: Yandi's creative direction shines in "Sore: Istri dari Masa Depan," a masterful expansion of the beloved series. The film, released in 2025, deeply enriches the intricate narrative, offering remarkable detail. Sheila Dara's portrayal of Sore is a standout, showcasing impressive character growth across multiple time loops. Despite its nearly two-hour runtime, the story feels incredibly dense and purposeful. This film deserves accolades for its compelling plot and Sheila Dara's powerful lead performance. The evocative scoring further elevates the emotional depth, making it a truly immersive experience.

I'm honestly so amazed by Yandy's work in Sore: Istri dari Masa Depan. The storyline and plot are brilliantly crafted - full of unexpected twists that keep you hooked from start to finish. Sheila Dara and Dion Wiyoko's performances were absolutely top-notch; their chemistry felt so real and emotionally gripping.

And the ending? So satisfying. It left me feeling genuinely relieved and fulfilled. This film truly deserves millions of viewers - it's the kind of movie everyone should experience at least once in their lifetime. So, so good.

Also... I was really moved by Sore's line: "Even if I had to repeat it a thousand times, I'd still choose you." UGH. That hit me right in the heart.

I came into this film with high expectations, after seeing its 8.9 IMDb rating and hearing it described as a "masterpiece" by many viewers.

And to be fair, Sore brings a few things to the table that deserve real praise.

The lead performance by Sheila Dara is outstanding - she brings emotional depth and vulnerability that anchors the entire film. Her acting is easily one of the film's strongest points.

The visual presentation is polished and beautiful, especially in the first half. And the premise itself is bold and different - a rare attempt at blending romance, sci-fi, and philosophical longing in Indonesian cinema. I truly appreciate the ambition behind it.

But despite all of that, the film falls short in one major area: storytelling clarity.

It tries to explore complex themes using a structure that involves time and memory, but never quite earns the audience's trust in how its world works. It leaves too many gaps, doesn't establish its rules clearly, and ultimately becomes hard to fully believe in - even if you're willing to suspend disbelief.

And I don't mean it has to be "realistic." Not at all.

But a story like this needs to feel internally logical - it has to make sense within its own universe. That's where this film stumbles.

I could see what the filmmakers were trying to achieve, emotionally and conceptually - and it's admirable. But concept without execution leads to frustration, not resonance.

Sore is a film with ambition, emotion, and standout performances - but also one that leaves you wishing it had taken more time to strengthen the foundation of its narrative logic.

If you're someone who values story mechanics as much as emotional impact, this might leave you more puzzled than moved.

Still, for what it dares to attempt - it deserves a watch.

This movie is a masterpiece by Yandy Laurens, surpassing all his previous works. Every scene feels like a painting crafted with heart, emotion, and soul. The story holds deep meaning and is filled with mysteries throughout, with plot points slowly unfolding one by one until it reaches a breathtaking climax. This isn't just a movie, it's a true masterpiece.

Now let's talk about the cinematography. Well, this is Yandy Laurens, your expectations won't be let down here. The acting? I could feel every emotion from all the actors. It's backed by a strong plot that's both complex and engaging to watch. And the choice of songs, the background music, it all fits the movie perfectly.

Maybe there's just one flaw, especially from a general audience's perspective. The beginning feels slow, and it might make you go, "What is this even about?" That actually happened when I watched it in the theater, the person sitting next to me was more focused on their phone than the movie. So yeah, this movie might not be for everyone. But for me, this is a true masterpiece.

A captivating film that excels in every aspect - from its breathtaking cinematography and well-crafted plot to its evocative soundtrack and deeply human character development. Watching it felt like being gently pulled into a world that mirrors both the beauty and complexity of real emotions.

By the time the credits rolled, I found myself on the verge of tears - not knowing whether they stemmed from joy, sorrow, or a quiet sense of fulfillment. It wasn't confusion, nor was it dissatisfaction with the ending, but rather a profound emotional resonance that lingered long after the screen faded to black.

This wasn't just a story being told; it was an emotional experience that speaks directly to the heart. Perhaps the finest example of drama and romance in Indonesian cinema - sincere, poignant, and unforgettable.
